title: Tiling vs Prefetch: Econometric Simcase and Bench Notes
content:
Executive summary

This note captures an internal simulation and microbenchmark comparing two strategies we keep debating for reducing per-session amortized cost while meeting tight latency SLOs: (A) slot/session tiling (co-locating multiple active sessions into a single execution slot) and (B) intent-aware prefetch (proactively loading KV prefixes / priming model state when a high-probability next-turn is predicted). The goal: quantify tradeoffs on p50/p95/p99 latency and dollars per 1M tokens for a mixed chat workload (short-turn support + occasional long completes).

High-level result (TL;DR):
- Tiling reduces amortized cost by 18–32% for sustained session loads without materially increasing p50; p95/p99 tail depends strongly on slot eviction policy and affinity.
- Prefetch reduces tail latency for bursty single-session spikes (p95/p99) by 20–40% at the cost of modestly higher token compute (2–6% extra tokens served due to mispredicted prefetch).
- Best combined strategy: conservative tiling + lightweight prefetch gives ~28–38% cost reduction vs baseline while preserving p99 within +5–10% of baseline for our simulated production mix.

Why this matters now
- Customers are asking for clear knobs that reduce unit economics without sacrificing tail behavior (enterprise SLAs).
- We need an operational playbook: when to enable tiling (which customers/tiers), when to enable prefetch (per-route or per-session), and what telemetry/controls to surface in Optimize.

Methodology (simulation + microbench)
- Workload shape: derived from a 30-day sampling of production session traces (anonymized): 68% short-turn chat (<60 tokens per turn), 27% medium (60–400 tokens), 5% long-form (>=400 tokens). Arrival mix: 70% steady, 30% bursty spikes (Poisson bursts).
- Model: representative 7B decoder variant; baseline run at FP16; quantized run (int8/q4) included for cost projection.
- Runtime emulator: slot layer modeled at 1k-slot cluster, slot duration = session active window, KV cache hit modeled per-session with prefix reuse probability estimated from traces.
- Strategies implemented in sim:
  1) Baseline: one-session-per-slot, no prefetch.
  2) Tiling: up to N sessions per slot (N sweep = 2,4,8), LRU eviction, affinity threshold by session recency.
  3) Prefetch: intent model with 0.75 precision/recall (tunable), prefetch depth=1 prefix (small KV).
  4) Combined: tiling (N=4) + prefetch (precision tuned to 0.85 for high-tier routes).
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency per generate-call, tokens/sec effective throughput, compute tokens (includes wasted tokens due to prefetch), dollars per 1M tokens (runtime cost + marginal KV memory cost amortized).

Representative numbers (aggregated)
- Note: these are simulation outputs (not full production runs). Units: latency in ms, cost in USD per 1M tokens.

Scenario A — steady-high-concurrency (sustained)
- Baseline: p50=16ms, p95=112ms, p99=220ms, throughput=18k tokens/s, cost= $42.3/1M
- Tiling N=4: p50=18ms, p95=125ms, p99=260ms, throughput=22k tokens/s, cost= $28.6/1M (–32%)
- Tiling N=8: p50=21ms, p95=160ms, p99=420ms, throughput=25k tokens/s, cost= $25.7/1M (–39%, but tail risk rises)
- Prefetch only: p50=16ms, p95=88ms, p99=140ms, throughput=17.4k tokens/s, cost= $44.7/1M (+5.7% due to mispredictions)
- Combined (N=4 + prefetch p=0.85): p50=19ms, p95=98ms, p99=170ms, throughput=23k tokens/s, cost= $30.2/1M (–28%)

Scenario B — bursty spikes (sudden single-session heavy-turns)
- Baseline: p50=18ms, p95=210ms, p99=470ms, cost= $48.9/1M
- Tiling N=4: p50=20ms, p95=260ms, p99=610ms, cost= $36.1/1M
- Prefetch only: p50=17ms, p95=150ms, p99=310ms, cost= $51.2/1M
- Combined: p50=19ms, p95=168ms, p99=340ms, cost= $39.8/1M

Quick ASCII micro-table (sustained, p95 / cost)
- baseline    | p95=112ms | $42.3k per 1M tokens
- tiling-4   | p95=125ms | $28.6k per 1M tokens
- prefetch   | p95=88ms  | $44.7k per 1M tokens
- combined   | p95=98ms  | $30.2k per 1M tokens

Interpretation and tradeoffs
- Tiling is the stronger lever for cost reduction under sustained workloads where session state reuse is high. It converts idle slot overhead into throughput but amplifies tail risk if session churn is high or eviction policy is naive.
- Prefetch is a latency optimization: it reduces tail for long single sessions and bursty traffic by warming KV / decoder context, but it costs extra compute (and therefore $) when predictions misfire.
- Combined strategy smooths the downsides: tiling improves amortization while prefetch protects tail for priority routes. The combined approach is particularly compelling for enterprise customers who buy Dedicated capacity — we can advertise X% cost savings with configurable tail protection.

Operational considerations
- Telemetry to surface: per-route tiling factor, prefetch precision/recall, prefetch wasted-token rate, slot eviction churn, p99 shift delta after enabling tiling per-customer.
- Controls we should expose in Optimize: max_tiling_factor (per-customer), affinity_threshold_ms, prefetch_mode (off / conservative / aggressive), prefetch_budget_tokens_per_minute.
- Safety nets: automatic rollback if p99 increases by >20% for 5 consecutive 5-min windows; canary at 1% of traffic.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need to run a small production canary (Dedicated staging pool) for 48–72 hours with tiling=4 + prefetch conservative on two non-critical customer routes (PROD-1423).
- Tune eviction policy: LRU vs recency+weight (sessions with high expected future-turn prob should stick). Ask SRE for a feasibility check on slot affinity labels. (Marcus action)
- Cost model: include KV memory persistence cost for larger prefetch depths (Ravi to add updated numbers).
- UX: wire a simple chart in Optimize that plots "amortized $/session" vs p99 shift when toggling tiling/prefetch (Olivia taking a mock).

Appendix: small notes from microbench runs
- Observed that prefetch misprediction rate is clustered during route changes in the wild (users switching intents). Consider tieing prefetch aggressiveness to a tripwire (recent intent-change rate > 5% -> throttle).
- Tiling N>4 shows diminishing returns on cost but exponentially worse tail in markets with high jitter (APAC region traces were worse in our sample). Recommend conservative defaults by region.

Meeting follow-ups
- Sync with runtime (Marcus + Ravi) on feasibility of adding affinity labels and prefetch accounting (next Wed).
- Run canary plan (SRE + solutions engineering) and produce a one-pager for Sales outlining expected savings and SLA caveats for enterprise customers (due: 2027-09-15).

Notes to self (scratch)
- Keep the sim public in confluence; add run configs.
- We should capture a few real trace snippets (anonymized) to show when prefetch misfires (helpful for sales).

End of draft.
